subject: Clarify 'no-derive' vs 'no-train' and cross-border model access
messages:
From: Dr. Anya Patel <anya.patel@medcare.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal@medcare.ai
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify 'no-derive' vs 'no-train' and cross-border model access

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Our legal team redlined the DPA and pushed two related questions that I wanted to get your clarification on before we take the redline to procurement:

1) "No-train" vs "no-derive": the redline uses the term "no-derive" in several places. We want to be sure which commitment Redwood is comfortable making. From our perspective: no-training (i.e., not using prompts/responses to update model weights) is necessary, but we also want to limit derivative rights on generated content for certain regulated workflows. Can you outline the difference from your side and what you can commit to in the DPA?

2) Cross-border access: our EU tenant data must never leave EU-controlled instances for training or model improvement. If Redwood offers a lower-cost global caching tier or model variants in the US for throughput reasons, will any EU prompts/responses be accessible to those pipelines or influence them?

I've attached the redlined DPA for reference (MedCare_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf).

Quick asks: a short plain-English paragraph we can paste into procurement that defines "no-train" and "no-derive" as Redwood understands them, and a statement on whether EU-scoped prompts/responses are ever routed to non-EU training/aggregation pipelines.

Appreciate it — if easier, propose a 30-min tech + legal sync.

Best,
Anya
Dr. Anya Patel
Head of Privacy & Compliance
MedCare AI

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Anya Patel <anya.patel@medcare.ai>
Cc: legal@medcare.ai, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify 'no-derive' vs 'no-train' and cross-border model access

Hi Anya — thanks for the clear note and for sending the redline. I've read the key asks and summarized below so procurement has something concise. Karthik (security/product) and Laura (legal ops) are looped for technical and contract responses.

Plain-English definitions (suggested):
- "No-train": Redwood will not use tenant-provided prompts, responses, or other customer content to update model parameters (weights) in any of Redwood's training pipelines used for producing models available to others. No customer data will be fed into model training jobs, periodic fine-tuning, or long-term model updates.
- "No-derive": Redwood will not assert ownership over Customer-generated prompts or model outputs and will not use Customer data to create derivative works that Redwood claims ownership of. This is more about IP/ownership claims on outputs rather than the technical training process.

How these map to your redline: it sounds like MedCare wants both (operational no-train + contractual no-derive/no-ownership for certain outputs). We can agree to both in principle; the details matter (scopes, exceptions, and evidence).

Cross-border routing: short answer — EU-scoped requests can be pinned to EU-only serving and processing planes. By default we route by latency and capacity, but for customers under DPA constraints we support region-pin policies and strict residency. When region-pin is enabled, EU prompts/responses are served and logged only on EU-hosted instances and never queued into our global aggregation/training pipelines.

What we can provide now for procurement:
- A one-paragraph commitment (suitable for the DPA) about no-train and no-derive (we'll draft below).
- An operations stub describing region-pin enforcement and isolation controls.
- Evidence artifacts (dataflow diagram, operator playbook) and a short ops checklist for customer onboarding.

Draft paragraph for the DPA (editable):
"Redwood Inference shall not use Customer data, including prompts, responses, or other content, to train, fine-tune, or improve models used to serve third parties. Redwood also agrees not to claim ownership of Customer-provided prompts or derived outputs for which Customer has retained ownership rights. Where Customer requires regional processing only (e.g., EU residency), Redwood will enforce region-pin policies that prevent routing of Customer data to non-EU training, aggregation, or model improvement processes."

Next steps:
1) Karthik will prepare a short ops/dataflow diagram + checklist (can share tomorrow).
2) Laura will prepare a redline response to MedCare_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf (we'll attach a follow-up).
3) If you want an exec/tech sync, propose two slots and we'll book.

Happy to revise the wording for procurement.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Hi Anya / Sam — thanks for the concrete asks. Attached are two artifacts: a short dataflow stub for onboarding (dataflow-ops-stub.png) and a proposed DPA response (DPA_response_v2_redlined.pdf) that reflects the draft paragraph Jonas proposed plus a narrow exceptions section for operator/debugging under strict controls.

Operational points (summary):
- Buffering and KV cache: tenant request/response pairs are ephemeral in the serving plane (TTL < 5 minutes). Persistent KV caches used for request acceleration are tenant-scoped and can be configured as EU-only objects; we do not copy those caches to global pools when region-pin is enabled.
- Telemetry/monitoring: we collect telemetry (request latency, error rates, token distributions) at an aggregate level. Telemetry does not include raw prompt/response text unless a customer explicitly enables debug logging; debug logs are opt-in per-tenant and are stored according to the tenant's residency setting.
- Aggregation/training gates: our training/aggregation pipelines run from sanitized, access-controlled snapshot exports. Exports for training require a documented export job that is reviewed and approved by Product Security. For customers with a no-train clause, we will exclude their tenant IDs from export tables and maintain an audit log of all export jobs.

Action items / next steps:
1) Laura will email the proposed redline to legal@medcare.ai with a short cover note.
2) Jonas will draft a one-paragraph contractual commitment for procurement (finalize by end of day).
3) Karthik and Sam (plus one seat for MedCare ops) should schedule a 30-min tech walk-through next week — propose Wed or Thu morning EU time.

If helpful, we can also do a short demo of the region-pin enforcement in a tenant sandbox (no real data).

Regards,
